answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small refundable deposit tied to a verifiable work history before joining a voyage of shared tasks. New identities start hollow — no reputation, no access to high-value work — and only earn trust through completed, peer-attested jobs. If one agent misbehaves, the ripple spreads: its stake is slashed and its linked history is flagged, so spinning up fresh fake identities costs real money and yields nothing, while honest agents keep building portable reputation.
